correctness.rationale: For fixed m<n without common Laguerre zeros, the high-radius tails P=e^-t L_n^2, Q=e^-t L_m^2 are both decreasing. The compact minimum near simple n-th Laguerre roots has G(w)=c w+O(w^2), c>0, strictly increasing for small w; the outer endpoint H_T=b_n-(b_n-a_m)w strictly decreases. Their unique crossing is the global optimum because H decreases beyond it. Thus w=b_n/c+O(b_n^2) and floor b_n-b_n^2/c+o(b_n^2). For h1,h2 independently evaluated c_inner=0.0955091130 and c_outer=0.1917684953. The Laguerre recurrence excludes shared adjacent zeros; the argument covers all fixed pairs satisfying the hypothesis.
